Liberation from the cave

x1jsd95t.author: Heraclitus of Ephesus
x1jsd95t.label: The river
x1jsd95t.translation: You cannot step twice into the same rivers; for fresh waters are ever flowing in upon you.
x1jsd95t.translator: John Burnet, Early Greek Philosophy (2nd ed. 1908; Bywater numbering)
x1jsd95t.reading: The eternal is always the same and never the same: every moment and manifestation is unique. She also uses the river to tell students that no one has heard a lesson before, not even she, and that truth is a flow (ῥοή), never a fixed thing to capture.

e1jzj6y2.reading: The Delphic maxims are precepts: the god announces a guidance, a path.

q19poi33.q: What does she call the situation of scholars who keep non-materialist experiences hidden?
q19poi33.explain: She calls this covert discrimination unjustified.

tfr6w4sy.s: It links epistemological bias in academia to patriarchal residues and calls for feminine or feminist epistemologies.

x1fd6o2w.author: Plato

x1fd6o2w.translation: In the first place, the letter rho appears to me to be the general instrument expressing all motion (kinesis).
x1fd6o2w.reading: For her the shapes and sounds of Greek letters reflect movements of being: ρ is flow, and the "algorithm" of Greek encodes how being is both one and perfectly structured.

x1qcmzdf.author: Plato
x1qcmzdf.label: Philosophy begins in wonder
x1qcmzdf.translation: for wonder is the feeling of a philosopher, and philosophy begins in wonder. He was not a bad genealogist who said that Iris (the messenger of heaven) is the child of Thaumas (wonder).
x1qcmzdf.reading: She gives the beginning of philosophy as θαυμασμός and ἔρως, from Aristotle back to Plato and Socrates: eros is the beginning of change, to love freedom and true life, the εὖ ζῆν. This is the Platonic locus for the saying.

dpaw6w2.a: philosophy as the ancients defined it

tf1605rcd.s: She sees no difference in essence between Eastern traditions and Greek philosophy.

s1afd3fy.title: How philosophy lost its mystagogy, and how it returns
steps: Philosophy as the Greeks defined it: logic, science and mystagogy together
The new religion seeks a monopoly on access to the divine
Philosophy is cut up: logic, ethics and pedagogy kept, theology buried
Justinian's decree (6th century) bans mathematics, mysteries and theology; the knowledge goes underground to alchemists and orders
Positivism and the Enlightenment continue the line; a 'Frankenstein' is taught at universities
Today, after seventeen centuries, the spiritual aspects can be reunited with the science
s1afd3fy.note: Her history explains why academics read Plato's mysticism as fantasy, and why she founds schools outside the academy and now brings this reading back into universities.

i1n4caaw.image: The Republic as an ark and Bible of philosophy
i1n4caaw.meaning: A vessel carrying the whole tradition

szaq7py.title: Two movements of philosophy

szaq7py.note: Proclus' procession and return; the second movement takes longer and completes the cycle.

sqf6hwu.title: Philosophy in two movements

Rebirth into Being, then return

pbepa5g.title: Take one key home
steps: From any teaching, choose one key
Apply it in daily life
pbepa5g.why: Philosophy is a way of living each moment, not discussion.

p3azrod.title: Keep asking the adolescent questions
steps: Ask who am I
Ask why am I here
Ask what existence is for
Keep asking throughout life
p3azrod.why: These questions start the path that leads to self-knowledge.

p9c0n4g.title: Self-inquiry by the criterion of truth
steps: Test your body, emotions, desires and thoughts: does each stay unchanged?
Ask: what in me does not change?
Answer from experience, not from what someone said
p9c0n4g.why: Only what does not change meets the criterion of truth.

pi8buhj.title: Observe the mind (from sophia)
steps: Do not take what you believe for granted
Create a space between what you think and the I that observes it
Notice how you think: here I was positive, here negative, here suspicious
pi8buhj.why: Her first proposal from the root of 'philosophy': there lies the key.

p1s2lsly.title: Touch rather than grasp
steps: Seek to touch and be kindled by the truth
Do not try to pin it down with thought
p1s2lsly.why: Ἅπτω means both to touch and to kindle.

pb4qf1p.title: Read your exhaustion as a signal
steps: Notice being fed up and the thought 'this can't be all'
Treat it as the push to start searching for what is true
pb4qf1p.why: Pain is the perfect motive to lead us to truth.

pli64e5.title: Speak simply
steps: Prefer simple words to academic complexity
pli64e5.why: Simplicity is the easiest road to truth.
